newsitem.title: BULGARIA: FOREIGN INVESTORS EYE HIGH-YIELD BULGARIA T-PAPER.
newsitem.headline: FOREIGN INVESTORS EYE HIGH-YIELD BULGARIA T-PAPER.

text.p: Foreign investors, attracted by high yields and pending sell-offs, have bought Bulgarian government securities worth 47 billion levs and $100 million, a central bank official said on Wednesday.

"Foreigners bought $100 million of bad debt bonds and some 47 billion lev worth of other treasury issues between the beginning of March and April 11," Nikolina Micheva, head of State Credits department at the central bank told Reuters.

Foreigners can invest in Bulgarian securities with maturity over six months through resident foreign banks and local ones according to Bulgarian laws. The 47 billion levs were invested in government securities with maturity of over six months.
"High yields and the stable lev/dollar exchange rate have encouraged foreign investment in government securities," Micheva said.
The Bulgarian National Bank's (BNB) main interest rate is now set at 14.15 percent monthly or 169.80 percent annually. This compares with a 12.3 percent monthly inflation rate in March.

The lev, which nosedived to 3,000 per dollar in February firmed after an interim cabinet took office two months ago. The lev recovered to around 1,500 now after trading around 1,600 in the past month.

A $1.2 billion financial support package pledged by international lenders recently and Bulgaria's plans to introduce a self-regulating fixed exchange rate mechanism, known as currency board, are expected to strengthen it further.

Both lev- and dollar-denominated bad debt bonds, known as Zunks, are accepted as means of payment in sell-offs at par value. Their minimum acceptable prices are now set at 35 and 45 percent of par, respectively.
Bad debt bonds worth 32 billion levs and $1.8 billion respectively were issued three years ago to cover banks' non-performing loans extended to state companies before 1991.
There were $939.6 million and 20 billion levs of bad debt bonds in circulation by the end of March, BNB figures showed.
The cabinet's first steps towards speeding up sell-offs to raise desperately needed cash, have also boosted Zunk trade.
The cabinet has decided to assign some big sell-offs to international investment banks instead of the privatisation agency, which so far has been too slow.
The BNB has sold 15.2 billion levs of lev-denominated Zunks from its portfolio in the first week of April, said Georgi Petkov, head of Lev Currency Operations department at the BNB.
"The fact that the paper was bought after interest payments on it have been made, gives us reason to think that the bonds are meant to be used in privatisation deals," Petkov said.

Sales of government securities from the BNB portfolio was part of preparations for introduction of the currency board, which bans central bank lending to commercial banks and the government and curbs open market operations, said Petkov. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
